note: A wider set of public-finance and economic indicators. Status (rising/falling/stable) describes the recent direction of the figure itself, not whether that direction is good or bad. Context matters and is left to the reader. Each record carries the date it was last verified against its own source. The ONS public sector finance, inflation, unemployment and productivity figures were re-verified on 22 September 2026; debt interest, growth, the tax burden and spending still carry their earlier dates. Spending is an estimate, and revenue is derived from it.

indicators.name: Debt as a share of GDP
indicators.explanation: Net debt measured against the size of the economy. Down 1.3 percentage points on a year earlier and at levels last seen in the early 1960s; over the past twelve months the ratio has stayed between 92% and 95% (September 2025 to August 2026, series HF6X: low 92.3% in January, high 94.9% in September).
indicators.source_name: ONS, Public sector finances, UK: August 2026

indicators.name: Borrowing as a share of GDP
indicators.explanation: Annual public sector net borrowing relative to the economy. The published outturn ratio for the financial year ending March 2026, on borrowing of £134.3bn, revised up from £129.8bn in the ONS annual alignment of September 2026. Down from 5.1% the year before.
indicators.source_name: ONS, Public sector finances, UK: August 2026 (series J5IJ, dataset PUSF)

indicators.name: Debt interest
indicators.explanation: The cost of servicing debt, relative to the economy. About £110 billion a year.
indicators.source_name: OBR, Economic and Fiscal Outlook March 2026

indicators.name: Inflation (CPI)
indicators.explanation: The rate at which consumer prices are rising over the year. Rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9% the month before.
indicators.source_name: ONS, Consumer price inflation, UK: August 2026

indicators.name: Unemployment rate
indicators.explanation: The share of people who want to work and are looking for a job but cannot find one. Up 0.2 percentage points on a year earlier and unchanged on the previous quarter.
indicators.source_name: ONS, Labour market overview, UK: September 2026

indicators.name: GDP growth
indicators.explanation: How fast the economy is growing, after adjusting for inflation. The 2026 forecast, down from 1.4% in 2025.
indicators.source_name: OBR, Economic and Fiscal Outlook March 2026 (real GDP growth forecast for calendar year 2026)

indicators.name: Productivity (output per hour)
indicators.explanation: How much is produced per hour worked, against a year earlier. Weak productivity growth limits how fast tax revenue can rise.
indicators.source_name: ONS, Output per hour worked, whole economy, % change on a year earlier, January to March 2026 (series LZVD, dataset PRDY, released 18 August 2026)

indicators.name: Tax burden
indicators.explanation: Total taxes as a share of the economy. Forecast to keep rising to the highest level since records began in 1948.
indicators.source_name: OBR, Economic and Fiscal Outlook March 2026

indicators.name: Government revenue
indicators.explanation: Total money the government receives, mostly from taxes. Derived by this site as spending minus borrowing until a published total replaces it, so a revision to borrowing moves this figure too.
indicators.source_name: Derived: HM Treasury PESA 2026 total managed expenditure (2025-26 outturn) minus ONS public sector net borrowing for 2025-26 (Public sector finances, UK: August 2026)

indicators.name: Government spending
indicators.explanation: Total money the government spends on services, benefits, investment, and debt interest.
indicators.source_name: HM Treasury, PESA 2026, Table 1.1, total managed expenditure, 2025-26 outturn
